## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** `hey`, `basecamp` and `cf` were the only unconditional `omarchy-mise-install` stubs in `install/user/mise.sh` missing from the `rm -f` list in `bin/omarchy-remove-preinstalls`. At bb0666e7 the list covers all 17. Their migrations already skip users with the `preinstalls-removed` marker, and Install Preinstalls restores them by rerunning `mise.sh` through `omarchy-refresh-applications`, so Remove and Install now act on the same set of stubs. Both testing claims in the description reproduce:

| `test/shell.d/preinstalls-test.sh` run against | Result |
|---|---|
| PR head | all 13 checks pass |
| base remover + PR test | fails with `hey is left behind` |
| head + an extra `omarchy-mise-install` line with no removal | fails, naming the new command |

Three smaller points follow. None of them affects the fix itself.

### Users who already opted out keep the three stubs

The change applies to future runs of Remove Preinstalls only. A user who ran it after these stubs were written (hey from 2026-08-20, basecamp from 2026-09-09, cf from 2026-09-13) keeps `~/.local/bin/{hey,basecamp,cf}` after updating, because no migration removes them:

```text
earlier Remove Preinstalls  -> marker written, hey/basecamp/cf left behind
update to this head         -> migrations 1787215824 / 1788941927 / 1789310715 skip (marker present)
                               no migration deletes the leftovers
menu                        -> "Remove Preinstalls" hidden while the marker exists (omarchy-menu.jsonc:297)
```

**Impact:** three stale wrappers remain for users who opted out during that window, with no menu route to clear them. Running the command directly still works.

**Suggested change:** a migration gated on the marker that removes each of the three only when the file is the wrapper `omarchy-mise-install` wrote, as migration `1786719479` does for the old `gemini` wrapper.

### Official hey and basecamp installers use the same path

The public `scripts/install.sh` in [basecamp/hey-cli](https://github.com/basecamp/hey-cli/blob/27f10faea1598b6310d9a21901043ff30d2e16a9/scripts/install.sh#L69-L86) and [basecamp/basecamp-cli](https://github.com/basecamp/basecamp-cli/blob/d91fc7b3ae5ee3c54a7fea389f59e791173e647b/scripts/install.sh#L91-L108) installs to `~/.local/bin` unless `~/bin` is on `PATH`. The `cursor-agent` and `muse` ownership checks in the same script exist for this kind of overlap. `mise.sh` already overwrites these paths unconditionally, so the PR is consistent with how the other 14 unconditional stubs are handled.

**Impact:** a user who replaced the Omarchy stub with the official `hey` or `basecamp` binary at that path now has it deleted by Remove Preinstalls. The binary can be reinstalled.

**Suggested change:** if the official installs should survive, use the `cursor-agent` pattern for these names: skip the stub in `mise.sh` when the command already exists, and remove it only when its content matches the generated wrapper. Otherwise no change is needed.

**Optional test improvement:** the new check passes while checking nothing when `grep` finds no lines. The process substitution's exit status is not seen by `set -e`, so a moved `mise.sh`, or `omarchy-mise-install` lines that no longer start at column 0, leave `stubs` empty. In diagnostic copies, both cases printed `ok`, including one with an unremoved extra stub. A guard after the loop closes this:

```bash
(( ${#stubs[@]} > 0 )) ||
  fail "Remove Preinstalls deletes every mise stub from the user setup" "no omarchy-mise-install lines found in install/user/mise.sh"
```

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR head and base, including the migrations, the menu entry and the restore path. `test/shell.d/preinstalls-test.sh` ran in an isolated sandbox with a private HOME, on the head, the base and labelled diagnostic copies. The full test suite, a live desktop and real mise installs were not run. The upstream installer scripts were read as source at the linked commits and were not executed. The suggested test guard and migration were not executed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
